scenes.text: Have you ever noticed that tiny, mysterious hole at the bottom of your airplane window, and did you know it is actually the only thing keeping you safe at thirty thousand feet?
As your plane climbs, the air pressure outside drops drastically, creating a massive amount of force that pushes against the cabin windows which are kept pressurized so you can comfortably breathe.
To stop the glass from shattering, these windows have three layers, and that tiny bleed hole in the middle pane carefully balances the pressure by redirecting the stress to the outer layer.
This simple hole also prevents the window from fogging up, but would you still fly if you saw it plugged? Tell me in the comments and follow for more secrets.
